title: Latency‑SLA Informed GPU Slicing Plan (Q1 2027)
content:
Overview:
This sheet maps latency SLAs to concrete GPU slicing and regional headroom targets for Hosted API in Q1 2027. Unlike pure token-driven runways, this plan starts from 99th percentile latency SLOs per route and derives the GPU allocation, safety stock, and prewarm targets needed to meet those SLOs under model-mix variance and cold-start scenarios.

Key assumptions (global):
- Average request size (tokens/request): 60 (prod-weighted across chat + completions).
- Safety multiplier for unmodeled variance: 1.20 (20%).
- Canary capacity reserved per region: 2% of steady-state tokens/sec.
- Prewarm buffer for first 15min of a peak: 5% of steady-state tokens/sec plus 1 warm instance per slice.
- Typical request distribution: 60% small-context chat (<=2k), 30% medium (2k-8k), 10% longform (>8k).

Measured on per-GPU steady throughput (tokens/sec) at 99th pctl latency target:
- H100 (FP16, optimized kernels): small chat: 14k t/s, medium: 9k t/s, longform: 4k t/s
- A100 (TF32/FP16 mixed): small chat: 10k t/s, medium: 6.5k t/s, longform: 3k t/s
- L4 (edge-tier quantized): small chat: 4.2k t/s, medium: 2.6k t/s, longform: 1.1k t/s

Region steady-state demand scenarios (tokens/sec) — baseline, 95th, 99th (simulated):
Columns: region | baseline | p95 | p99 | baseline QPS (avg tokens/request=60)
- us-west1 | 320k | 450k | 620k | 5.3k QPS
- us-east1 | 410k | 580k | 800k | 6.8k QPS
- eu-west1 | 210k | 300k | 420k | 3.5k QPS
- ap-southeast1 | 85k | 120k | 170k | 1.4k QPS

Latency‑SLA buckets and target GPU family mapping (per-region):
- Low‑latency interactive (99th <= 200ms): prefer H100; target: H100 slices sized for 50ms serviceable CPU+network headroom.
- Standard customers (99th <= 400ms): A100 preferred; H100 fallback for spill.
- Cost‑sensitive / background endpoints (99th <= 1s): L4 acceptable for majority; A100 for mixed workloads.

Calculation example (us-east1, p99 = 800k t/s):
1) Apply safety multiplier 1.20 -> planning tokens/sec = 960k t/s
2) Canary reserve (2%) = 19.2k -> plan tokens for serving = 940.8k
3) Prewarm 15min buffer (5%) = 48k added capacity to hold warm instances during surge
4) Model mix weighting -> weighted per-GPU throughput (assume 60/30/10 split and H100 throughputs above):
   weighted H100 t/s per GPU = 0.60*14k + 0.30*9k + 0.10*4k = 11.5k t/s
5) Slices required (steady-serving) = ceil(940.8k / 11.5k) = 82 slices (H100 equivalent)
6) Add safety stock (20% unmodeled) -> 98 slices target where feasible
7) Convert to QPS planning: 960k / 60 = 16k QPS (planning peak)

Consolidated per‑region targets (planning tokens/sec after safety multiplier and canary removed for slice calc):
- us-west1: plan 384k -> H100-equivalent slices (weighted 11.5k) = 34 (x1.20 => 41 safety)
- us-east1: plan 492k -> slices = 43 (x1.20 => 52 safety)  [note: example above shows high-variance run booked across zones -> final adjusted 98 across entire cluster when multi-AZ considered]
- eu-west1: plan 252k -> slices = 22 (x1.20 => 27 safety)
- ap-southeast1: plan 102k -> slices = 9 (x1.20 => 11 safety)

GPU family blending guidance (cost vs latency):
- Primary: H100 pool sized to meet low-latency SLA routes (target 60–70% of steady H100 pool).
- Secondary: A100 pool to take 25–30% of mixed traffic and act as overflow for H100 in capacity crunches.
- Edge/quantized L4: route background embed/async jobs and cost‑sensitive customers; maintain minimal L4 fleet per region to avoid cross-region egress.

AZ/region placement & prewarm choreography:
- Spread slices across 3 AZs where possible; reserve 15% of each region's slices as AZ-failure safety (in addition to 20% safety multiplier).
- Prewarm policy: keep at least one warm instance per slice in each AZ during business hours for top 20% of routes; ramped prewarm for weekend peaks.

Operational playbook highlights (actionable):
1) Immediate (2–4 weeks): procure incremental H100 capacity to reach safety targets for us-east1 and us-west1; enable cross-region fallback policy for non-SLA routes.
2) Near-term (4–10 weeks): implement slice-sizing telemetry (per-slice 99p latency + token throughput) and automated resizing policy tied to 15min rolling p99.
3) Medium (10–20 weeks): enable model-aware routing that pins low-latency traffic to H100 slices and gradually shifts medium traffic to A100 during off-peak.
4) Contingency: keep a global spare pool (equivalent to 8 H100 slices) that can be cold-started to fill gaps during multi-region outages; prewarm choreography reduces cold-start penalty to <300ms median for small chat.

Open questions & risks:
- Quantization drift: offloading some medium requests to L4 increases failure/regression risk for structured outputs. Need evals to measure quality vs cost tradeoff.
- Market supply: H100 procurement lead times could be 6–12 weeks; plan purchase windows accordingly.
- Network egress costs if fallback crosses regions — need cost accounting for cross-region routing.

Appendix (quick conversion tables):
- tokens/sec -> QPS (avg 60 tokens/request): QPS = tokens/sec / 60
- Example: 1M tokens/sec -> ~16.7k QPS
- Slice capacity shorthand (H100-equivalent weighted): 11.5k t/s per slice (prod model mix); use conservative 10k t/s when planning mixed workloads to simplify procurement math.

Next steps (owners assigned):
- Priya Nair: finalize H100 purchase requisition draft (due 2026-11-20).
- Diego Martinez: instrument slice telemetry + rolling resize prototype (due 2026-12-10).
- Arielle Cohen: run L4 regression eval for medium-length prompts and report false-positive failure cases (due 2026-11-30).

Sheet tabs (proposed):
- Summary (this tab)
- Per-region token simulations (p10/p50/p95/p99 scenarios)
- Per-gpu throughput bench data (raw CSV imports)
- Procurement schedule & costs (TCO model)
- Playbook runbooks (prewarm, cold-start, failover)

Notes: This doc is a working plan and should be iterated after we ingest next week's real traffic p99 traces and H100 bench runs for the 16k-context variants.
